subject: Metered->Commit conversion and tiered overrun accountability
messages:
From: Tariq Ahmed <tariq@clearwave.ai>
To: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@clearwave.ai
Date: Tue, 22 Jul 2025 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Metered to committed conversion & short-term overrun accountability

Hi Mina —

Quick context: we have a product launch scheduled Aug 12 and expect token usage to spike for ~4 weeks as we scale. Right now we’re on metered billing and would like to convert to a committed plan, but need a short-term safety lane for the launch so we don’t get throttled while procurement finishes PO/commit approvals.

Ask: can Redwood provide a provisional headroom (buffer) for the launch window and clarify how overrun true-ups would be handled if we exceed the provisional buffer? Specifics we care about:
- Can the buffer be a prepaid credit or a temporary soft quota?
- How will overrun be billed (rate multiplier, reconciled month-end, or converted to committed tokens)?
- Any minimum notice or procurement PO steps required to avoid abrupt throttles?

I’ve attached our traffic_report_q2.csv and a draft SLA from our side for reference. We’re aiming to move to a 12-month commit after the launch if the numbers look stable.

Thanks — Tariq
Tariq Ahmed
Head of Platform | Clearwave Labs
attachments: traffic_report_q2.csv, SLA_draft.pdf
From: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>
To: Tariq Ahmed <tariq@clearwave.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 22 Jul 2025 10:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Metered to committed conversion & short-term overrun accountability

Tariq — thanks for the note and the data.

High-level proposal so we can unblock the launch:
1) Provisional headroom: we can provision a 6-week buffer sized at 20% above your forecast for August as a prepaid credit that applies only to overrun charges. That credit will be consumed first and then normal overrun billing applies.
2) True-up cadence: monthly true-up at the end of the billing cycle. Any remaining prepaid buffer credit will be rolled forward once (one-cycle) if you move to a committed plan within 30 days of the launch period.
3) Conversion incentive: if Clearwave signs a 12-month commit within 60 days, we’ll apply a one-time onboarding discount of 10% on the first three months of committed usage (applied as credit).
4) Overrun rate: overrun beyond prepaid buffer will be billed at the current metered rate unless you accept a temporary elevated overrun multiplier (1.5x) in exchange for a reduced committed rate later — we can structure this as part of the term sheet.

Next steps: I’ve attached a short conversion_term_sheet_v1.pdf. Ben/Jordan — please review pricing language and confirm whether the buffer should be billed as prepaid credit (preferred) or a temporary soft quota.

Mina Haddad
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
attachments: conversion_term_sheet_v1.pdf

Subject: Re: Metered to committed conversion & short-term overrun accountability

Tariq / Mina / Ben —

I reviewed the term sheet and ran numbers with finance/legal. My recommendations to keep both sides protected:
- Buffer mechanics: make it a prepaid credit (applied to overrun) that appears on the invoice as a separate line item. If unused at month-end and Clearwave converts to a 12-month commit within 30 days, we roll forward unused credit once. If not, unused balance is forfeited.
- Pricing tiers (for the commit):
  * 250k tokens/month commit -> 5% discount off metered list
  * 1M tokens/month commit -> 12% discount off metered list
  * 1.5x overrun multiplier applies to usage beyond prepaid buffer if no commit is signed within 60 days of the launch window
- Audit/evidence: require weekly token usage export and the Redwood meter logs as the source-of-truth for any disputes. We can automate a shared Drive folder with CSVs.
- Procurement/PO: Accept a PO to enable the provisional buffer. However, final pricing/commit needs a signed DocuSign term sheet to trigger the 12-month discounts.

I attached a simple pricing_grid.csv for clarity. If Clearwave is comfortable, Mina — please send PO template language we can accept and I’ll prepare DocuSign.

Jordan Blake
Head of Revenue Ops | Redwood Inference
attachments: pricing_grid.csv
